prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: proposed smithy interior visual mockup for Blobber / Stone & Shadow, a first-person C++ grid-based dungeon crawler. Generate one wide 16:9 landscape image. This is planning artwork for approval, not a runtime screenshot.
Input images: reference image 1 is the actual inn game capture, for modest furniture scale, broad unobstructed walking routes, simple textured geometry and palette. Reference image 2 is the inn's painted interior concept, for cohesive hand-painted fantasy material language. Create a different room: a working smithy.
Primary request: a compact, welcoming but work-worn medieval fantasy blacksmith shop belonging to the same Sanctuary town as this inn. Eye-height first-person view from just inside the entrance, straight ahead into a rectangular room. Readable simple grid-aligned layout, believable ordinary-human scale, no huge furniture. Warm grey limestone block walls with some pale aged lime plaster between dark oak beams, a low timber-beamed ceiling and small worn grey stone floor flags. Crisp low-poly geometry with detailed painted, subtly pixelated textures; more like a feasible classic dungeon-crawler environment than a cinematic illustration.
Layout: back-left wall contains a broad soot-darkened stone forge with a small orange coal fire on a waist-low work bed and a chimney hood rising to the ceiling. A modest anvil on a short timber block stands near the forge, offset to the left, with a small quench tub beside the wall. Keep the central approach from the entrance to the rear counter generously open and flat. A low, shallow wooden service/work counter sits toward the rear centre-right, well BELOW the viewer's eye line. Behind it leave a clearly visible empty staff standing area facing the entrance, large enough for one future human blacksmith NPC: open floor, no stool, no armor mannequin, no props or shelves in that standing volume. This is the central future conversation position, readily visible from the entrance. Put rear tool shelves and a tidy hammer/tongs rack along the wall beyond that staff aisle. The counter should not extend wall-to-wall: a simple open passage at its right end allows the smith to reach the forge. Modest weapon rack with a few swords and a shield on the right wall; a few iron stock bars and a small charcoal bin clustered at the left perimeter. Small recessed shuttered window admits gentle daylight from the right. Objects sit against walls or on compact coherent workstations. Sparse useful detail rather than clutter.
Composition/framing: clear full-room entrance view at normal standing human eye height, natural mild downward framing with horizon around 40 percent from the top, no ultra-wide lens distortion, no aerial/isometric/cutaway view. Forge left, reserved NPC station rear centre-right, equipment display right. Show floor circulation and a complete unobstructed human silhouette space above and behind the rear counter. Anvil top around human knuckle height, counter around human waist height; avoid the oversized counter problem seen in many game concepts.
Lighting/mood: warm muted honey-brown wood, grey stone, dull iron, restrained orange forge glow and cool window daylight. Warm shading painted into textures, restrained believable lighting. Small contained forge flame only, no sparks filling the room, no dramatic bloom, no volumetric haze. Still maintained and in use.
Constraints: empty environment with NO people or NPCs; reserve their future standing space architecturally. No HUD, no labels, no annotations, no text, no logo, no watermark, no weapons held by the viewer. No inn tables, rugs, plants, staircase or bar-drink decor. No photorealistic PBR, no glossy metal, no elaborate high-poly machines, no extravagant cathedral height or cavernous hall, no stairs or raised walking platforms. Match the inn's handmade painted world while making the smithy's function unmistakable.
